svg.title: Level 3 Comprehensive: an official statistics publication
svg.desc: Level 3 Comprehensive: an official statistics publication. Stages run across and lanes run down. An official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics, which NHSBSA's Analytical Assurance Decision Tool gives as a worked example of impact 3. Drawn here at Level 3 Comprehensive, which is where impact 3 lands at high likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work. Stages, left to right: Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis, Delivery and sign-off and Review. Commissioner. Owns the question and the resource. Engagement and scoping: State the decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Score the impact with the analyst, and record Business Critical status either way. Design: Approve the design before work proceeds. Protect the assurer's time in the schedule, and allow for a re-review. Analysis: Stay available. Review any change of design or method, and resist changing the question late. Delivery and sign-off: Confirm it meets the need you commissioned it for, apply its limitations, and approve it for release. Review: Own the review with the analyst, annually, on any material change, and before any reuse for a new purpose. Analyst. Owns the method and the write-up. Engagement and scoping: Clarify the real question. Record the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions in a formal commissioning record. Design: Choose the method, score the likelihood and read your level. Agree the assurance plan with an assurer from outside your team, and specify the verification and validation. Analysis: Do your own checks first. Keep an assumptions register, log decisions as you go, and quantify the uncertainty where the method allows. Delivery and sign-off: Write it up with the caveats in the output itself, and publish the quality assurance statement with its uncertainty ranges. Review: Record the lessons where the next analyst will look, and share the method beyond the delivering team. Critical friend. At Level 3, an assurer from outside the delivering team. Design: You are named at design, not found at delivery. Confirm the approach answers the question and that the assurance planned is right. Analysis: Reproduce the calculations from source and assure the code. Read the documentation as a document, not only the numbers, and report back. Delivery and sign-off: State what you assured: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented. You are giving advice, not signing it off. Review: What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping. Lead Official for Statistics. Signs the work off at Level 3, and the route for advice on official statistics. Engagement and scoping: You are named before the work starts, not found at delivery. Delivery and sign-off: Sign the output off, and set the review date. None: This lane is empty at Design, Analysis and Review. What is handed over. 1: Commissioner to Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. 2: Analyst to Critical friend, at Design. The assurance plan, with the assurer from outside the team named on it. 3: Critical friend to Analyst, at Analysis. Findings, which are the analyst's to act on. 4: Analyst to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results, so they are understood before sign-off. 5: Analyst to Lead Official for Statistics, at Delivery and sign-off. The output, the published statement and the assurance evidence. 6: Lead Official for Statistics to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Signed off, for release with the statement. Why this one is Level 3 Comprehensive: NHSBSA's worked examples put an official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics, at impact 3, alongside Principal Component Analysis, a Board report, an FOI response and a ministerial briefing. High visibility raises how much assurance the work needs, and on its own it does not make the analysis Business Critical, so there is no Analysis Senior Responsible Officer in this lane. Level 2 added separation from the work. Level 3 adds separation from the team, full verification and validation, code assured, uncertainty quantified where the method allows, and the statement published with the output. The Lead Official for Statistics signs it off, a review date is set, and review is annual. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.

div.b: Level 3 Comprehensive: an official statistics publication

div.span: An official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics, which NHSBSA's Analytical Assurance Decision Tool gives as a worked example of impact 3. Drawn here at Level 3 Comprehensive, which is where impact 3 lands at high likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work.
Owns the question and the resource

div.div: State the decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Score the impact with the analyst, and record Business Critical status either way.
Approve the design before work proceeds. Protect the assurer's time in the schedule, and allow for a re-review.
Stay available. Review any change of design or method, and resist changing the question late.
Confirm it meets the need you commissioned it for, apply its limitations, and approve it for release.
Own the review with the analyst, annually, on any material change, and before any reuse for a new purpose.

div.span: Owns the method and the write-up

div.div: Clarify the real question. Record the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions in a formal commissioning record.
Choose the method, score the likelihood and read your level. Agree the assurance plan with an assurer from outside your team, and specify the verification and validation.
Do your own checks first. Keep an assumptions register, log decisions as you go, and quantify the uncertainty where the method allows.
Write it up with the caveats in the output itself, and publish the quality assurance statement with its uncertainty ranges.
Record the lessons where the next analyst will look, and share the method beyond the delivering team.

div.div: You are named at design, not found at delivery. Confirm the approach answers the question and that the assurance planned is right.
Reproduce the calculations from source and assure the code. Read the documentation as a document, not only the numbers, and report back.
State what you assured: appropriately scoped, executed, validated, verified and documented. You are giving advice, not signing it off.
What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids.

div.span: Signs the work off at Level 3, and the route for advice on official statistics

div.div: You are named before the work starts, not found at delivery.
Sign the output off, and set the review date.

div.span: 1. Commissioner → Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be
2. Analyst → Critical friend, at Design. The assurance plan, with the assurer from outside the team named on it
3. Critical friend → Analyst, at Analysis. Findings, which are the analyst's to act on
4. Analyst → Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results, so they are understood before sign-off
5. Analyst → Lead Official for Statistics, at Delivery and sign-off. The output, the published statement and the assurance evidence
6. Lead Official for Statistics → Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Signed off, for release with the statement

div.b: WHY THIS ONE IS LEVEL 3 COMPREHENSIVE

div.span: NHSBSA's worked examples put an official statistics publication, such as Dental Statistics, at impact 3, alongside Principal Component Analysis, a Board report, an FOI response and a ministerial briefing. High visibility raises how much assurance the work needs, and on its own it does not make the analysis Business Critical, so there is no Analysis Senior Responsible Officer in this lane. Level 2 added separation from the work. Level 3 adds separation from the team, full verification and validation, code assured, uncertainty quantified where the method allows, and the statement published with the output. The Lead Official for Statistics signs it off, a review date is set, and review is annual.
